'''''Echeveria pulidonis''''' is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Crassulaceae]], [[native plant|native]] to central [[Mexico]], more specifically, Puebla and Veracruz.<ref name="dortort">Dortort, Fred (2011). "The Timber Press Guide to Succulent Plants of the World". Timber Press. {{ISBN|9780881929959}} (hardback).  p. 80</ref>
[[File:Echeveria Puldonis.jpg|thumb|An Echeveria Pulidonis being grown as a houseplant]]

==Description==
'''Habit:''' Forms rosettes of leaves, and as it ages, it will naturally form offsets, creating clusters of rosettes. Each rosette can reach 13–15 cm in diameter.<ref name="dortort" />

'''Leaves:''' Tapered to a sharp point. Green with red margins.<ref name="dortort" />

'''Flowers:''' Yellow.<ref name="dortort" />
<gallery mode=packed   heights="240px">
(MHNT) Echeveria pulidonis inflorescence.jpg|Inflorescence
</gallery>

==Cultivation==
Half-hardy. Dislikes water sitting on its leaves, but tolerates this more than some other ''Echeveria'' species do.<ref name="dortort" />

== Taxonomy ==
''Echeveria'' is named for [[Atanasio Echeverría y Godoy]], a botanical illustrator who contributed to ''Flora Mexicana''.<ref name="gledhill">Gledhill, David (2008). "The Names of Plants". Cambridge University Press. {{ISBN|9780521866453}} (hardback), {{ISBN|9780521685535}} (paperback).  pp. 149</ref>
